requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a HEADERS frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode and recognize the 8-bit frame Type as 0x01.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not identify a frame with another Type value as a HEADERS frame.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded frame type is directly inspectable.

requirements.quote:
Unused Flags (2),
     PRIORITY Flag (1),
     Unused Flag (1),
     PADDED Flag (1),
     END_HEADERS Flag (1),
     Unused Flag (1),
     END_STREAM Flag (1),
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing the HEADERS frame flags octet.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the specified one-bit positions for PRIORITY, PADDED, END_HEADERS, and END_STREAM, with the other four bits unused.
requirements.why_checkable: The eight flag-bit positions can be checked directly in serialized frames.

requirements.quote: [Pad Length (8)],
requirements.condition: When a HEADERS frame contains a Pad Length field.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent Pad Length as an 8-bit field.
requirements.why_checkable: The field width is observable in the payload encoding.

requirements.quote:
Pad Length:  An 8-bit field containing the length of the frame
      padding in units of octets.  This field is only present if the
      PADDED flag is set.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a HEADERS frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Interpret Pad Length as the padding length in octets and include it only when PADDED is set.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not include the Pad Length field when PADDED is not set.
requirements.why_checkable: Field presence and its relationship to the padding length and PADDED flag are directly testable.

requirements.quote:
Exclusive:  A single-bit flag.  This field is only present if the
      PRIORITY flag is set.  Priority signals in HEADERS frames are
      deprecated; see Section 5.3.2.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a HEADERS frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent Exclusive as one bit and include it only when PRIORITY is set.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not include the Exclusive field when PRIORITY is not set.
requirements.why_checkable: The field width and conditional presence can be verified from serialized payloads.

requirements.quote:
Stream Dependency:  A 31-bit stream identifier.  This field is only
      present if the PRIORITY flag is set.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a HEADERS frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent Stream Dependency as a 31-bit stream identifier and include it only when PRIORITY is set.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not include the Stream Dependency field when PRIORITY is not set.
requirements.why_checkable: The width and conditional presence of the field are directly inspectable.

requirements.quote:
Weight:  An unsigned 8-bit integer.  This field is only present if
      the PRIORITY flag is set.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a HEADERS frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent Weight as an unsigned 8-bit integer and include it only when PRIORITY is set.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not include the Weight field when PRIORITY is not set.
requirements.why_checkable: The field type, width, and conditional presence can be tested.

requirements.quote: Field Block Fragment:  A field block fragment (Section 4.3).
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a HEADERS payload.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the Field Block Fragment as a field block fragment.
requirements.why_checkable: The payload component can be checked using the implementation's field-block parser or encoder.

requirements.quote:
Padding:  Padding octets that contain no application semantic value.
      Padding octets MUST be set to zero when sending.  A receiver is
      not obligated to verify padding but MAY treat non-zero padding as
      a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When sending a HEADERS frame with padding.
requirements.required_behavior: Set every padding octet to zero.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send a non-zero padding octet.
requirements.why_checkable: Outbound padding bytes can be inspected for zero values.

requirements.quote:
Padding:  Padding octets that contain no application semantic value.
      Padding octets MUST be set to zero when sending.  A receiver is
      not obligated to verify padding but MAY treat non-zero padding as
      a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When receiving a HEADERS frame containing non-zero padding.
requirements.error_behavior: The receiver may treat the frame as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR; it is not required to verify the padding.
requirements.why_checkable: A crafted frame with non-zero padding can verify either permitted receiver behavior.

requirements.quote:
PRIORITY (0x20):  When set, the PRIORITY flag indicates that the
      Exclusive, Stream Dependency, and Weight fields are present.
requirements.condition: When the HEADERS PRIORITY flag 0x20 is set.
requirements.required_behavior: Include and parse the Exclusive, Stream Dependency, and Weight fields.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not omit any of those three fields.
requirements.why_checkable: The flag value and all three corresponding payload fields are directly observable.

requirements.quote:
PADDED (0x08):  When set, the PADDED flag indicates that the Pad
      Length field and any padding that it describes are present.
requirements.condition: When the HEADERS PADDED flag 0x08 is set.
requirements.required_behavior: Include and parse the Pad Length field and the number of padding octets it describes.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not omit the Pad Length field or described padding.
requirements.why_checkable: The flag, length field, and padding presence can be checked in encoded payloads.

requirements.quote:
END_HEADERS (0x04):  When set, the END_HEADERS flag indicates that
      this frame contains an entire field block (Section 4.3) and is not
      followed by any CONTINUATION frames.
requirements.condition: When the HEADERS END_HEADERS flag 0x04 is set.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the HEADERS frame as containing the entire field block.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not follow it with CONTINUATION frames for that field block.
requirements.why_checkable: Frame sequences and field-block completion state can be observed.

requirements.quote:
A HEADERS frame without the END_HEADERS flag set MUST be followed
      by a CONTINUATION frame for the same stream.  A receiver MUST
      treat the receipt of any other type of frame or a frame on a
      different stream as a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type
      PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: After a HEADERS frame without END_HEADERS set.
requirements.required_behavior: The next frame must be a CONTINUATION frame on the same stream.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not interleave another frame type or a frame on a different stream.
requirements.why_checkable: The immediately following frame's type and stream identifier can be tested.

requirements.quote:
A HEADERS frame without the END_HEADERS flag set MUST be followed
      by a CONTINUATION frame for the same stream.  A receiver MUST
      treat the receipt of any other type of frame or a frame on a
      different stream as a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type
      PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When a HEADERS frame without END_HEADERS is followed by any non-CONTINUATION frame or by a frame on another stream.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat receipt as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: Malformed frame sequences can be injected and the connection-level error response observed.

requirements.quote:
END_STREAM (0x01):  When set, the END_STREAM flag indicates that the
      field block (Section 4.3) is the last that the endpoint will send
      for the identified stream.
requirements.condition: When the HEADERS END_STREAM flag 0x01 is set.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat this field block as the endpoint's last field block for the identified stream.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The endpoint must not subsequently send another field block for that stream.
requirements.why_checkable: Subsequent outbound field blocks on the identified stream can be detected.

requirements.quote:
A HEADERS frame with the END_STREAM flag set signals the end of a
      stream.  However, a HEADERS frame with the END_STREAM flag set can
      be followed by CONTINUATION frames on the same stream.  Logically,
      the CONTINUATION frames are part of the HEADERS frame.
requirements.condition: When a HEADERS frame has END_STREAM set and its field block continues.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit same-stream CONTINUATION frames and treat them logically as part of the HEADERS frame before completing the stream-ending field block.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reject those CONTINUATION frames merely because END_STREAM is set.
requirements.why_checkable: A fragmented END_STREAM HEADERS sequence can test whether continuation processing remains allowed.

requirements.quote:
The frame payload of a HEADERS frame contains a field block fragment
   (Section 4.3).  A field block that does not fit within a HEADERS
   frame is continued in a CONTINUATION frame (Section 6.10).
requirements.condition: When a field block does not fit within one HEADERS frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Continue the field block in a CONTINUATION frame.
requirements.why_checkable: Encoder output can be checked for CONTINUATION framing when the block exceeds the HEADERS capacity.

requirements.quote:
HEADERS frames MUST be associated with a stream.  If a HEADERS frame
   is received whose Stream Identifier field is 0x00, the recipient MUST
   respond with a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type
   PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When sending or processing a HEADERS frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Associate the HEADERS frame with a non-zero stream identifier.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use stream identifier 0x00 for a HEADERS frame.
requirements.why_checkable: The stream identifier in every HEADERS frame is directly inspectable.

requirements.quote:
HEADERS frames MUST be associated with a stream.  If a HEADERS frame
   is received whose Stream Identifier field is 0x00, the recipient MUST
   respond with a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type
   PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When a HEADERS frame with Stream Identifier 0x00 is received.
requirements.error_behavior: Respond with a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A zero-stream HEADERS frame can be injected and the required connection error observed.

requirements.quote:
The HEADERS frame changes the connection state as described in
   Section 4.3.
requirements.condition: When processing a HEADERS frame.
requirements.why_checkable: The referenced state change is not specified within this chunk, so the precise implementation behavior cannot be derived here.

requirements.quote:
The total number of padding octets is determined by the value of the
   Pad Length field.  If the length of the padding is the length of the
   frame payload or greater, the recipient MUST treat this as a
   connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When parsing a padded HEADERS frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Use the Pad Length value as the total number of padding octets.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not infer a different padding length.
requirements.why_checkable: The parsed padding extent can be compared directly with the encoded Pad Length value.

requirements.quote:
The total number of padding octets is determined by the value of the
   Pad Length field.  If the length of the padding is the length of the
   frame payload or greater, the recipient MUST treat this as a
   connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When the declared padding length is equal to or greater than the HEADERS frame payload length.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat the frame as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: Boundary and over-boundary Pad Length values can be supplied and the resulting connection error observed.

requirements.quote:
The PRIORITY frame (type=0x02) is deprecated; see Section 5.3.2.  A
   PRIORITY frame can be sent in any stream state, including idle or
   closed streams.
requirements.condition: When sending or receiving a PRIORITY frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit the frame in any stream state, including idle and closed.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reject it solely because the stream is idle or closed.
requirements.why_checkable: PRIORITY frames can be exercised in each stream state and acceptance observed.

requirements.quote: Length (24) = 0x05,
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a PRIORITY frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Use a 24-bit Length field with value 0x05.
requirements.why_checkable: The serialized length field is directly inspectable.

requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a PRIORITY frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode and recognize the 8-bit frame Type as 0x02.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not identify a frame with another Type value as a PRIORITY frame.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded type byte is directly inspectable.

requirements.quote: Unused Flags (8),
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a PRIORITY frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat all eight flag bits as unused by the PRIORITY frame.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not assign PRIORITY-frame semantics to any flag bit.
requirements.why_checkable: Flag handling can be tested across all flag-bit values.

requirements.quote:
Exclusive (1),
     Stream Dependency (31),
     Weight (8),
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing a PRIORITY frame payload.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode the payload as a 1-bit Exclusive field, a 31-bit Stream Dependency field, and an 8-bit Weight field in that order.
requirements.why_checkable: Field widths and ordering are directly verifiable in the five-octet payload.

requirements.quote: Exclusive:  A single-bit flag.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing the Exclusive field of a PRIORITY frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent Exclusive as a single-bit flag.
requirements.why_checkable: The field width is directly inspectable.

requirements.quote: Stream Dependency:  A 31-bit stream identifier.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing Stream Dependency in a PRIORITY frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent Stream Dependency as a 31-bit stream identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: The field width and interpretation are directly testable.

requirements.quote: Weight:  An unsigned 8-bit integer.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing Weight in a PRIORITY frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent Weight as an unsigned 8-bit integer.
requirements.why_checkable: The permitted encoded range and width are directly testable.

requirements.quote: The PRIORITY frame does not define any flags.
requirements.condition: When interpreting a PRIORITY frame's flags field.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the frame as defining no flags.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not attach PRIORITY-frame semantics to flag bits.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's behavior for set flag bits can be tested.

requirements.quote:
The PRIORITY frame always identifies a stream.  If a PRIORITY frame
   is received with a stream identifier of 0x00, the recipient MUST
   respond with a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type
   PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When sending or processing a PRIORITY frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Associate the PRIORITY frame with a non-zero stream identifier.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use stream identifier 0x00 for a PRIORITY frame.
requirements.why_checkable: The stream identifier is directly observable in the frame header.

requirements.quote:
The PRIORITY frame always identifies a stream.  If a PRIORITY frame
   is received with a stream identifier of 0x00, the recipient MUST
   respond with a connection error (Section 5.4.1) of type
   PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When a PRIORITY frame with stream identifier 0x00 is received.
requirements.error_behavior: Respond with a connection error of type PROTOCOL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A zero-stream PRIORITY frame can be injected and the connection error observed.

requirements.quote:
Sending or receiving a PRIORITY frame does not affect the state of
   any stream (Section 5.1).  The PRIORITY frame can be sent on a stream
   in any state, including "idle" or "closed".  A PRIORITY frame cannot
   be sent between consecutive frames that comprise a single field block
   (Section 4.3).
requirements.condition: When sending or receiving a PRIORITY frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Leave the state of every stream unchanged.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not transition a stream solely because a PRIORITY frame was sent or received.
requirements.why_checkable: Stream state can be recorded before and after PRIORITY processing.

requirements.quote:
Sending or receiving a PRIORITY frame does not affect the state of
   any stream (Section 5.1).  The PRIORITY frame can be sent on a stream
   in any state, including "idle" or "closed".  A PRIORITY frame cannot
   be sent between consecutive frames that comprise a single field block
   (Section 4.3).
requirements.condition: When a stream is in any state, including idle or closed, and no field-block frame sequence is being interrupted.
requirements.required_behavior: Permit a PRIORITY frame to be sent on that stream.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reject the frame solely due to the stream state.
requirements.why_checkable: Frame handling can be exercised in every stream state.

requirements.quote:
Sending or receiving a PRIORITY frame does not affect the state of
   any stream (Section 5.1).  The PRIORITY frame can be sent on a stream
   in any state, including "idle" or "closed".  A PRIORITY frame cannot
   be sent between consecutive frames that comprise a single field block
   (Section 4.3).
requirements.condition: While consecutive frames are carrying one field block.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send a PRIORITY frame between those consecutive frames.
requirements.why_checkable: Outbound frame ordering during fragmented field blocks can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
A PRIORITY frame with a length other than 5 octets MUST be treated as
   a stream error (Section 5.4.2) of type FRAME_SIZE_ERROR.
requirements.condition: When a PRIORITY frame declares a payload length other than 5 octets.
requirements.error_behavior: Treat the frame as a stream error of type FRAME_SIZE_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: PRIORITY frames with invalid declared lengths can be injected and the stream error observed.

requirements.quote: Length (24) = 0x04,
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing an RST_STREAM frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Use a 24-bit Length field with value 0x04.
requirements.why_checkable: The serialized length field is directly inspectable.

requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing an RST_STREAM frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Encode and recognize the 8-bit frame Type as 0x03.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not identify a frame with another Type value as an RST_STREAM frame.
requirements.why_checkable: The encoded type byte is directly inspectable.

requirements.quote: Unused Flags (8),
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing an RST_STREAM frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat all eight flag bits as unused by the RST_STREAM frame.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not assign RST_STREAM-frame semantics to any flag bit.
requirements.why_checkable: Flag handling can be tested across all flag-bit values.

requirements.quote: Error Code (32),
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing an RST_STREAM payload.
requirements.required_behavior: Represent Error Code as a 32-bit field.
requirements.why_checkable: The field width is directly visible in the four-octet payload.

requirements.quote:
The Length, Type, Unused Flag(s), Reserved, and Stream Identifier
   fields are described in Section 4.  Additionally, the RST_STREAM
   frame contains a single unsigned, 32-bit integer identifying the
   error code (Section 7).  The error code indicates why the stream is
   being terminated.
requirements.condition: When encoding or parsing an RST_STREAM frame.
requirements.required_behavior: Include exactly one unsigned 32-bit integer error code that identifies why the stream is being terminated.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not omit or duplicate the error-code field.
requirements.why_checkable: The number, width, signedness, and use of the payload field can be checked in the frame codec.

requirements.quote: The RST_STREAM frame does not define any flags.
requirements.condition: When interpreting an RST_STREAM frame's flags field.
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the frame as defining no flags.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not attach RST_STREAM-frame semantics to flag bits.
requirements.why_checkable: The implementation's behavior for set flag bits can be tested.
